nutshell: A volatile session for individual stocks amid inflation fears.

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: This is the closing bell briefing for February 28th. It was a sea of red across the board today. The major indices all finished in negative territory.

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: That's right. Today's market can be summed up as 'a volatile session for individual stocks amid inflation fears.' The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell over 1% to close at 48,977.92, and the Nasdaq Composite also slipped about 0.9% to 22,668.21. The S&P 500 was also down 0.4%, ending the day at 6,878.88. The backdrop for this broad decline was a hotter-than-expected Producer Price Index report.

sources.title: ppi mom

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: So even though the indices were all down, you're saying there were some very different stories playing out with individual companies. What happened there?

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: Yes, we saw some companies move in the complete opposite direction of the broader market. A prime example is the fintech company Block, which surged over 20% after announcing massive layoffs driven by its adoption of AI. We also had some M&A news shaking up the media sector. Netflix jumped more than 13% after it dropped its bid for Warner Bros. Discovery, which the market saw as a move that resolved uncertainty. Paramount Skydance, now the likely winner, also rallied over 20%. On the flip side, Warner Bros. Discovery's stock fell more than 2%, so we saw a real mix of fortunes there.

sources.title: Jack Dorsey's Block cuts roughly 50% of jobs as it embraces AI and shares jump
Netflix Drops Warner Bros. Bid, Leaving Paramount the Winner

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: I see. So it was a day where major internal corporate changes drove individual stock moves, despite pressure from macro data. Could you break down the key themes that moved the market today?

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: Certainly. Two main currents dominated the market today. First, the concern that a higher-than-expected inflation report could lead to a prolonged period of tight monetary policy. And second, major M&A and restructuring news from a few companies that bucked the market trend. Let's dive into each of these themes now.

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: Alright, let's start with that first theme you mentioned: the inflation data. So a hot Producer Price Index really put a drag on the market.

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: Yes, it was the scenario the market was most worried about. The January Producer Price Index, or PPI, released yesterday morning, came in much hotter than expected, signaling that the fight against inflation is far from over. The month-over-month increase was 0.5%, well above the 0.3% consensus estimate. And Core PPI, which excludes volatile food and energy, came in at 0.8%, more than double the forecast. On that news, the major indices came under pressure, with the S&P 500 falling 0.8% and the Dow dropping 1.4%. The bond market also reacted sharply. The 10-year Treasury yield saw some volatility during the session, ultimately closing around the 3.96% level. This suggests the Fed's path to rate cuts could be much bumpier, which also acted as a tailwind for the dollar. On top of that, oil prices also rose amid geopolitical tensions, adding to concerns about cost-push inflation.

Stock market today: Dow, S&P 500, Nasdaq sink after hot PPI inflation print, indexes on track for monthly losses

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: So basically, the big fear that hit the market was that the Fed's timeline for rate cuts could be pushed back even further.

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: That's exactly right. This PPI data showed that inflation has a 'sticky' quality—it doesn't just go down in a straight line, it can pop back up. As a result, the prevailing analysis is that the Federal Reserve now has absolutely no reason to rush into cutting rates. Market expectations for a rate cut in the first half, particularly in May or June, have significantly receded. The consensus is now shifting toward the first cut not happening until the second half of the year. This uncertainty weighed heavily on growth stocks, especially rate-sensitive tech stocks. The technology sector fell over 1.6% today, leading the market lower. In contrast, the utilities sector, a classic defensive play, rose over 1%, showing a clear rotation by investors toward safer assets amid the market volatility.

sources.title: Fed's Rate Cut Timeline Pushed Back After Stubborn Inflation Report
Why the 'Last Mile' of Inflation Is the Hardest for the Fed

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: Now that we've confirmed this 'sticky' inflation, I imagine the upcoming inflation reports will be even more critical.

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: Yes, that's right. All eyes in the market are now turning to the Personal Consumption Expenditures, or PCE, price index, which is the Fed's preferred inflation gauge. The next PCE report is scheduled for March 13th, and its importance has grown even more after this PPI shock. If the PCE also comes in hot, it could not only delay rate cuts but also bring talk of potential further rate hikes back to the table. On the other hand, if the PCE comes in cooler than expected, it could offset some of this PPI shock and give the market some room to breathe. So, until that next PCE release, the market is likely to remain volatile, moving more on company-specific earnings and news rather than a clear overall direction.

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: As you said, it was a day where individual company news really stood out amid the macro uncertainty. The M&A news in the media sector, in particular, caught the market's attention. Let's take a closer look at that.

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: Right. Today's market was a clear demonstration of how individual corporate narratives can create divergence in stock performance, even in a down market driven by macro data. Unfazed by the broader sentiment, the media companies at the center of a major M&A battle and the fintech firm Block, which announced a bold restructuring powered by AI, both saw their stocks surge on their own positive news, capturing all the market's attention.

sources.title: ppi mom
Netflix, Paramount shares jump as months-long fight for Warner Bros ends
Jack Dorsey’s Block Slashes Nearly Half Its Staff in AI Bet

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: So the news was that Netflix pulled out of the bidding war for Warner Bros. Discovery. But isn't backing out of a deal usually seen as a negative that creates uncertainty? Why did the stock jump more than 13%?

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: In this case, the market viewed it as a major positive because it eased fears of a costly 'winner's curse.' Netflix officially stated that it withdrew because the bidding war had become overheated and the deal was no longer financially attractive. In fact, the offer from the Paramount Skydance consortium was $31 per share, significantly higher than the $27.75 Netflix had proposed. Investors reacted positively to the fact that Netflix avoided a costly bidding war and can now focus its massive capital on its core business, like content creation. That's what sent the stock higher. Conversely, Paramount, now the likely winner of the bidding war, surged over 20% on expectations of the powerful content library and expanded market dominance it would gain by acquiring Warner Bros. Meanwhile, the target company, Warner Bros., fell over 2% because the prospect of a higher bid from a strong contender like Netflix was now off the table.

sources.title: Netflix, Paramount shares jump as months-long fight for Warner Bros ends

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: So the market's cost-benefit analysis for each company in the deal was clearly reflected in their stock prices. And then you have the fintech company Block, which you mentioned surged over 20% on news of an AI-driven restructuring?

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: Yes, Block's case is a perfect example of how enthusiastic Wall Street is right now about the combination of 'artificial intelligence' and 'cost efficiency.' CEO Jack Dorsey announced a bold restructuring to cut about 4,000 jobs, explaining that the decision was based on a firm belief that AI will change the future of labor productivity. The key was his vision to run the company more efficiently using internally developed AI tools like 'Goose.' The market interpreted this not just as a simple cost-cutting measure, but as a declaration that Block intends to fundamentally transform its business model with AI. This comes after a recent Citi Research report raised concerns that AI could threaten the payments industry. Block, however, showed it's tackling that threat head-on by turning AI into an opportunity, allowing its stock to post a standout gain even as the broader tech sector fell.

sources.title: Jack Dorsey’s Block Slashes Nearly Half Its Staff in AI Bet

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: So the key takeaway is that despite the broader market weakness, companies with powerful individual narratives like M&A or AI were able to forge their own path. Let's move on to some other notable company moves.

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: First up is Morgan Stanley. The stock caught a lot of attention today, falling more than 4% and even dipping to the $164 level at one point. What happened with this Wall Street giant?

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: Right, Morgan Stanley saw significant volatility today as two completely contradictory stories collided. On one hand, management announced a full-scale push into the digital asset space—covering Bitcoin custody, trading, and lending—presenting a new engine for future growth. But on the other hand, one of Morgan Stanley's own top strategists put out a bearish note, warning that the market is 'crashing under the surface.' This clash of narratives created confusion among investors, and the stock ultimately ended the day with a steep decline.

sources.title: Morgan Stanley 'Absolutely' Plans to Offer Bitcoin Custody, Trading, Yield and Lending: Exec
This Expert Says the S&P 500 Has 'Crashed Under the Surface.' What a Stealth Correction Means.

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: So you have an announcement about a future growth driver coming out at the same time as an internal warning. Let's start with the positive side. Isn't there a view that this move into digital assets is an innovative opportunity?

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: Absolutely. Investors focused on growth potential see this announcement not just as adding a new business line, but as a bold attempt to own the operating system of future finance. They believe Morgan Stanley can leverage its decades of brand trust and regulatory experience to offer a level of stability that existing crypto firms can't match, potentially allowing them to dominate the market. The plan to build a complete ecosystem—going beyond simple trading to include custody, deposits, and lending—is creating excitement that this could be a game-changer, allowing them to attract massive client assets that currently exist outside their platform and create a new growth curve.

sources.title: Morgan Stanley 'Absolutely' Plans to Offer Bitcoin Custody, Trading, Yield and Lending: Exec

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: But despite that potential for future growth, the stock plunged, which must mean the market sees the risks as being much greater. What specific risk factors were highlighted?

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: Yes, that was the core concern for the market today. The bearish view is that the risks of this new venture are asymmetrically high compared to the potential rewards. The biggest concern is 'reputational contagion' risk. Morgan Stanley's core strength is the 'trust' built by its wealth management division, which manages over $9 trillion in assets. The fear is that if a single major incident—like a large-scale hack or a regulatory breach—occurs in the crypto business, the shock could create a fatal crack in the credibility of their core business. This is a risk that could shake the very foundation of the company.

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: So you're saying the risk from the new business could threaten the stable, core business. Is there any way to quantify the scale of that risk?

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: It's difficult to predict precisely, but the potential impact is substantial. According to their 2025 annual report, the Wealth Management division is the company's pillar, accounting for about 46% of total net revenues. One analysis suggests that if reputational damage caused just 0.5% of the assets in this massive division to leave, the permanent loss in fee revenue could more than offset all the potential profits expected from the new crypto business. Ultimately, the market seems to be questioning whether it's a rational decision to risk the company's most important asset—its 'trust'—for what might be minimal additional revenue. The view is that today's stock drop could be the start of a rational repricing of this structural risk.

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: Alright, if you could sum up today's market action in one sentence, what would it be?

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: It was a day of relief as inflation data came in as expected, but also one of cautious optimism about the path ahead. The January Personal Consumption Expenditures, or PCE, price index released today met market expectations, allowing Wall Street to avoid an inflation shock. As a result, all three major indices closed with modest gains in a sigh of relief. However, aggressive buying was limited as investors remain aware that the Fed's path to rate cuts is still uncertain. Ultimately, you can see a strong underlying sentiment in the market of wanting to confirm that the disinflationary trend will continue.

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: Now that we're past the major hurdle of the PCE report, where will the market's focus turn next?

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: The market's attention will now shift to indicators that directly show the strength of the economy. The ISM Manufacturing PMI, set to be released next Monday, and the Services PMI on Wednesday will be particularly important. These indices show whether the manufacturing and service sectors are in an expansion or contraction phase. Right now, the market wants to see if the economy is maintaining a 'Goldilocks' state—not too hot, not too cold. If the data comes in stronger than expected, it could raise fears of prolonged Fed tightening, while data that's too weak could spark concerns about a recession.

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: When you talk about the economy's strength, I assume the jobs market data is the most important piece of the puzzle, right?

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: Exactly. The February jobs report, due out next Friday, will be the most critical turning point after the PCE release. Investors will be watching the non-farm payrolls number, the unemployment rate, and the average hourly earnings growth. Wage growth, in particular, is one of the metrics the Fed watches most closely as it's directly linked to inflation. Given that the much stronger-than-expected January jobs report sent a shock through the market, whether the labor market remains hot in February or shows the gradual cooling the Fed wants to see will be the key variable determining the market's direction from here.

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: I see. And finally, what's one key takeaway for investors to keep in mind?

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: The market is likely to remain in a data-dependent mode for the time being, reacting sensitively to each new piece of information. The important thing is not to get swayed by short-term fluctuations in the data, but to confirm whether the bigger picture—of slowing inflation and a gradually rebalancing labor market—remains intact. With expectations for the timing of the Fed's rate cuts constantly shifting, this is a time for prudence and managing portfolios based on confirmed data, rather than making premature bets.

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: Thank you for your insights today. That wraps up our closing bell briefing for February 28th.
